Asked in the mosque whether Abu Talha had sent him to invite him to a meal, Anas said yes, and the Prophet told his companions to get up and go.
Abu Bakr hosted three poor Suffa companions but stayed late with the Prophet; when they ate, the food increased from beneath, and it was taken to the Prophet.
Companions the Prophet sends out may accept due hospitality from their hosts, and take a guest's right from those who refuse it.
When an extra man followed the Prophet to Abu Shu'aib's meal for five, the Prophet left it to the host to admit or refuse him, and he admitted him.
Seeing hunger on the Prophet's face, Abu Shu'aib had a meal for five made; when a sixth man followed, the Prophet left it to him, and he admitted the man.
A guest is owed a day and night's best food and three days' hospitality, without overburdening his host; Salman would not eat alone, nor Abu Bakr's guests without him.
